By achieving <cite id="4">a cost per beneficiary of $9.08</cite>, the charity stretches funds across large beneficiary bases. Combined with its <cite id="2">clear zakat policies</cite>, the organization provides a tailored outlet for faith-based giving directed at severe humanitarian crises.
rich_narrative.summary: BASMAH operates humanitarian relief operations primarily focused on Rohingya refugees and vulnerable populations in Bangladesh, providing medical care, food distribution, and education programs <cite id="4">since its founding in 2018</cite>. The organization reported <cite id="3">$4,195,860 in total revenue in 2023</cite>, reflecting steady growth with a <cite id="3">3-year revenue CAGR of 42.1%</cite>. BASMAH maintains clear religious alignment for Muslim donors through <cite id="2">verified zakat-eligible programs</cite> that serve designated asnaf categories like the poor and needy. However, <cite id="3">no financial filings newer than FY2023 are available — donors should treat this 3-year-old financial picture with caution</cite>. Furthermore, its <cite id="3">0.8 months of working capital reserves</cite> present liquidity risks, and its board governance metrics show significant gaps. On the operational side, BASMAH demonstrates significant cost efficiency in its direct service delivery, maintaining <cite id="4">an estimated cost per beneficiary of $9.08</cite> across its relief programs.
